source: GeoFM meta-analysis workbook v4 (V. Mancoridis, unpublished): 14,600 reported scores from 52 papers. Summary statistics only; no individual scores.
method: Scoring follows 'GeoFM Benchmark Scoring' (S. Wang, Oct 2026). A task is one paper's comparison of >= 4 GeoFMs on one benchmark, protocol, metric and training fraction (original results only; ablations, non-foundation baselines and from-scratch rows dropped). tau2_obs = variance of model scores within the comparison (observed separation). sigma2 = replicate noise of one evaluation: the median over models of the squared seed/run SD, from per-seed values listed in the cell (GEO-Bench v2 leaderboard) or a printed mean +/- sd, when >= 3 models in the comparison have one (measured); otherwise a plug-in from the same dataset, protocol family and metric (still counted as measured for the dataset), or the protocol-family median seed SD for points-scale metrics (provisional). tau2 = tau2_obs - sigma2/n_reps, where n_reps is the number of replicates behind each reported mean (seed-list length, the count the paper states, or 3 assumed; 1 for provisional tasks); EDI = tau2/sigma2; score = tau2/(tau2+sigma2) in [0,1]: the share of observed model spread that is repeatable. score_top repeats this on the leading half of each comparison (at least 4 models): the frontier score. A dataset's score is the model-count-weighted mean over its measured comparisons (provisional ones if none is measured); 90% intervals bootstrap the models within each comparison. The latent-factor regression y = mu_t + lambda_t'theta_m + eta is fit by alternating ridge least squares on standardised imagery tasks; K is chosen by held-out-cell cross-validation (one-SE rule on RMSE). unexplained_share = stable variation not captured by the K factors (diagnostic, not a penalty). info_share = Monte-Carlo Shapley share of log det(I + Lambda'C^-1 Lambda), the redundancy-adjusted information the dataset adds about shared capabilities.

verdicts.e_reliable: Reliable discriminator: >= 80% of the model spread is repeatable (measured seed noise)
verdicts.e_moderate: Moderate: 50-80% of the spread is repeatable (measured seed noise)
verdicts.e_weak: Weak or saturated: < 50% of the spread exceeds measured seed noise
verdicts.e_prov_high: Provisional: >= 80% repeatable under plug-in noise (no printed seed SD)
verdicts.e_prov_low: Provisional: < 80% repeatable under plug-in noise (no printed seed SD)
verdicts.e_spread: Spread only: no noise estimate, so reliability cannot be assessed
verdicts.e_few: Scored, but fewer than 4 models in any one comparison

latent.K_selection: smallest K within one SE of the best held-out RMSE, stepped down until bootstrap geometry stability >= 0.5
